column3: “The land” does not explicitly retain dryness; “rose” renders the flower name.
“Anxious” renders the hasty or alarmed heart.
“Once” supplies a temporal description for the jackals’ lying place.
“Only” is supplied; the final clause is rendered as fools not straying onto the way rather than not going astray on it.
“Crowned” replaces the description of everlasting joy upon their head.
